title: Is There a Double Standard for World Cup Criticism?
author: Team Zeteo
content:
How beautiful will the beautiful game be this summer, when the World Cup has
already been mired by [exorbitant](https://www.cnn.com/2026/06/06/sport/world-
cup-friendlies) ticket prices, a [criminal complaint
](https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49001477/platini-files-criminal-
complaint-fifa-infantino)against FIFA's new president, and of course, entry
and [visa chaos](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/08/world/africa/somalian-
world-cup-referee-denied-us-entry.html) caused by U.S. President Donald
Trump's vicious crackdown on Middle East and African countries? And are there
double standards in the way Western media reacted to recent world cups versus
this one?

In this new three-part, deep-dive video series, **Zeteo 's** editor-in-chief
and lifelong[ Liverpool and England football
fan](https://x.com/mehdirhasan/status/1916228482323091500?lang=en) **Mehdi
Hasan** sets out to answer those questions.

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

Mehdi goes back in history to explain how some of the world's most shameful
leaders have used the World Cup and FIFA's corrupt behavior to raise their own
status on the world stage and also distract from their country's heinous human
rights violations - a practice known as
**[sportswashing.](https://www.theguardian.com/football/gallery/2024/dec/11/a-history-
of-world-cup-sportswashing)**

In this first episode, Mehdi starts off with an authoritarian whose
sportswashing is not getting nearly enough attention right now: U.S. President
Donald Trump - one of the co-hosts of this summer's World Cup, despite his
administration having [threatened](https://www.nbcnews.com/sports/soccer/ice-
may-world-cup-matches-us-rcna344797) to bring rogue ICE agents to the World
Cup stadiums.

Throughout this series, Mehdi is also joined by a team of expert guests, like
former football player turned political scientist **Jules Boycoff** , Human
Rights Watch Global Initiatives Director **Minky Worden,** and New Yorker
Global Affairs Columnist **Ishaan Tharoor.**
